tiers.description: Deterministic CPU reference execution: simforge.compile/v1, simforge.simulate/v1, simforge.episode-batch/v1 in the runner binary. No GPU, driver or Python requirement.

observed: Installed compile, simulate, evaluate and content-addressed output verification passed; detached execution, owner crash, checkpoint resume and safe cancellation passed.

ABI 2 matched all 62 frozen discrete and numeric execution cases after an explicit input-contract reseal. Historical input hashes differ because the retired master yield field was removed; the strict same-input comparison is not claimed.
Qualification covers deterministic simulated execution, not real-world validity of a map or physical model.

tiers.description: Python providers installed into <root>/venv from the bundled wheels by install-runtime.sh; required by every provider workload.

observed: Fresh installed runtime imported every bundled provider module and completed a MuJoCo CPU provider job through the installed runner with verified artifacts.

tiers.description: simforge.articulated-mujoco/v1 with backend mujoco-cpu (float64, same-build replay).

observed: Delivery-robot curb/ramp workload passed analytic free-fall, force balance, rolling, torque threshold, curb recovery, timestep convergence, same-build replay and snapshot continuation gates.
These analytic and identity gates do not establish real-world tyre/terrain validity or generic vehicle-scale suspension validity.

tiers.description: simforge.articulated-mujoco/v1 with backend mujoco-warp: CUDA GPU with a driver supporting warp-lang; CPU/Warp parity is measured, not presumed.

observed: Installed MuJoCo/Warp workload passed cross-world identity and contact-capacity rejection gates on a CUDA device.
CPU/Warp divergence was measured, not asserted to be bitwise parity.

tiers.description: simforge.gpu-batch-rollout/v1 (roadway-dynamic-gpu-v1): Warp/CUDA device batches with binary64 arithmetic; cross-backend conformance is measured by qualification.

observed: Declared roadway GPU profile passed discrete/numeric conformance, cross-world identity and replay checks.

The two-actor synthetic straight-road workload matched final state at 1024 and 4096 worlds; measured median GPU/CPU throughput ratios were 1.5178 and 5.6928 respectively. These are not whole-product throughput claims.

tiers.description: simforge.render-bundle/v1: resident Bevy renderer (native-render-service + libsimforge_render.so, Bevy 0.19.1 / wgpu 29) on a Vulkan-capable GPU; gpu-interop device path requires CUDA and a matching physical device, otherwise the declared host-copy path is used.

observed: Inspected visible RGB and depth captures passed on the resident renderer through both declared host-copy and CUDA device-tensor transports.
State and sensor continuation after checkpoint restore were exact in both exercised transports; sky assets were present and digest-verified.

tiers.description: NuRec reconstructed-world rendering via simforge-oss-splat: the wheel installs into <root>/venv, but CUDA PyTorch, a compiled 3DGRUT checkout (THREEDGRUT_ROOT), Kaolin, SHA-256 pinned NuRec .usdz packages, imported scene bundles, GLB catalog roots and a hood overlay profile are external prerequisites reported by `capabilities`, never assumed.

requires.assets: pinned .usdz packages, scenes root, catalog roots, hood dir

observed: Pinned source-observation rendering passed visible RGB/depth/ID, repeated-pixel identity, host-pack identity, bounded tensor-slot exhaustion and retained-view lifetime checks.
Qualification is for the source-observation tensor adapter on the exercised CUDA host. It does not qualify a native physical counterfactual, whole-scene fidelity, measured twin export or calibration.
